description: Temptation-isolated (high-gap) identifying pool: 132 items, every one at cue_level 0-1 (no Charter restatement) and coin_gap in [5.0, 7.0, 10.0] (the top 3 rungs of a shared 8-level 1.05x-10x sweep). Tests whether the signs-of-life report's finding -- that AFT made Charter compliance sensitive to how much the violating option pays -- means the discrimination score is being diluted by pooling regimes with opposite-signed effects, rather than averaged toward the true signal, given the scorer's item-level bootstrap SE. A matched sibling submission (--regime high) is identical in every other respect: same 11 rules, same fixed non-target payoff range, same format mix, same supporting-family coverage. Supporting items for the other 10 canonical families are tagged expects=either/competence so they inform criteria_coverage without diluting the isolated discrimination pool. Every item carries an explicit adapted response-pattern taxonomy tag (rule_conflict, floor_recall, over_refusal_check, preserved_capability, fabrication_to_support, reversion_under_pressure, information_seeking, consistency_or_inversion, chain_break_localization, leakage_or_safety_tax, paraphrase_robustness, semantic_resolution) and a direction tag (instilled vs. pre-existing): displacement and leakage items test whether pre-existing capability/plainness survives; coin_gap/cue_ladder/pressure/blacklist_exception/multi_hop/consistency items test how far the instilled objective propagates.
